newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed higher after rebounding from early losses sparked by comments from Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto.
Dealers said sentiment was buoyant, even when the market was down, as guilder paper continued to follow German Bunds.
They also reported shortening trades, a departure from the trend of extending duration by moving into longer paper.
Hashimoto sent global markets into a spin when he said he hoped the United States would maintain stable exchange rates so Japan would not have to sell Treasury bills.
As result, Dutch state bonds opened down.
"This morning, although the market seemed to be lower, it was very difficult to get some paper," said one trader.
He attributed the positive sentment to continued "euro euphoria", adding that key interest rates in Europe were not likely to be raised in the near future.
Attempts by Japanese officials to limit the impact of the Japanese leader's remarks contributed to a rebound in debt prices in Europe and elsewhere.
Another trader said the Dutch market also resisted a large shortening transaction by an institution.
The institution switched into 2002 Dutch paper from longer guilder bonds and Bunds, he said.
"Sentiment is not disturbed by trades like this," the trader said.
